chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Saʿdān, from Ḥakam, from a man, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him: May a man urinate while he is standing? He said: “Yes, but it is feared that the Shayṭān may become mixed up with him—that is, confound him.” Then I said: May a man urinate in water? He said: “Yes, but it is feared for him from the Shayṭān.”

key_terms.يَلْتَبِسَ: to become entangled or mixed up with
key_terms.يُتَخَوَّفُ: it is feared; there is apprehension of harm
key_terms.يُخَبِّلَهُ: to confound him or disturb his state

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a man to urinate while standing or in water in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses etiquettes related to relieving oneself, indicating that urinating while standing or in water is permissible in principle. However, it warns that such acts are feared to expose a person to harm from the Shayṭān, showing a discouragement rooted in etiquette and spiritual caution.
